Rava-Ruska New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Lviv Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Presumed to have operated from the early 20th century, this cemetery served a community present since the city's 1624 founding and home to several Hasidic courts, including ones founded by members of the Rokeach dynasty in the 1920s. Its Jewish population peaked around 6,100 — over half the town — by 1910, before wartime occupation brought a ghetto absorbing refugees from surrounding villages and, by its December 1942 liquidation, the execution or deportation of thousands. The cemetery itself is presumed demolished after the war, though never built over; a memorial using recovered gravestone fragments was erected near a mass grave in the 2010s.
